items.title: Final Fantasy XIV FanFest in Tokyo reveals new Job, full trailer, and more!
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV’s next expansion is creeping up on us, so that means we get another FanFest, and the final one before Evercold, no less. A few hours ago
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV’s next expansion is creeping up on us, so that means we get another FanFest, and the final one before Evercold, no less. A few hours ago in Tokyo, Japan, producer and director Naoki Yoshida stepped out on stage to reveal more of this new instalment of the Warrior of Light’s adventures, including the premiere of the full trailer for the game, the second new Job, and – most excitedly – a release date.

First was the full trailer for the expansion, which I’ve thrown above. Not only is this gorgeous, with an incredible first listen of the full theme for Evercold, but it does pose a lot of questions about the expansion. What can the Warrior of Light do to aid the Fourth? What are the worryingly clean-looking robots flying around the world? Who is the mysterious woman that looks suspiciously like Ysayle? When did Estinien learn that incredible dropkick?

Obviously though, the big reveal is the second new Job coming with Evercold, the crossbow and bird-wielding Zephyr. Falling into the ranged melee DPS, this Job will start at level 90 and will be obtainable in Gridania. It appears to have some fun mobility options, and Yoshi-P outlined that it will have party support utility, so this might be the new Job for me in Evercold after I lost that bet at Berlin FanFest.

The next big reveal was that we finally have a release date! It’s roughly three weeks later than the team wanted, but Yoshida really pressed the point that they wanted a little more time to polish certain elements of the game. Therefore, the tentative release date for Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold will be Tuesday 23 rd February 2027, with Early Access beginning on Friday 19 th February.

Additionally, we got more information about game features such as the new Raid difficulty, now titled “Fierce”, which will fit between Normal and Savage difficulty. This segment also showed more of the areas you will be exploring in the Fourth, more information around the updated gameplay systems like the Evolved Combat Mode, a reminder about the Collector’s Edition of the game, and new concept and key art for the expansion.

Finally, we got to get another look at the upcoming crossover Raid series for Evercold, the Evangelion content titled Ghosts of Desire. The new trailer gave us basically no new information, but it looked pretty damn good nonetheless. I think I’m happy to go into this unseen to be honest, so the lack of reveals for this sits nicely with me, especially as we saw so much during this keynote address already.

So, in summary, we had the following revealed over the keynote:

Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold is creeping ever closer now, with that 23 rd February release date only a few months away. The journey to the Fourth looks to be an exciting one for the Warrior of Lights both in-game and out, and I genuinely cannot wait for it. Will you be picking up the new expansion, or making the switch to Zephyr or the other new Job, Bastion? And what did you think of the FanFest Tokyo keynote?

Bad news for impatient fans: Square Enix has just confirmed that Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold , the MMORPG's next major expansion, will arrive later than originally anticipated. Previously scheduled for January 2027, the sixth expansion has been pushed back to February 23, 2027 . The revised date was announced during the latest Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival in Tokyo. Early access is scheduled to begin on February 19, four days before the official release, while pre-orders open on November 4.

Despite the delay, Square Enix has provided plenty of new information about the expansion. A new full-length trailer was recently unveiled alongside additional footage showcasing locations, dungeons and upcoming content. The publisher also revealed Zephyr, the second new job coming to Evercold . The ranged fighter combines crossbow attacks with assistance from an avian companion named Nephele. Zephyr joins Bastion, the previously announced tank-focused job, expanding the available options for players.

Evercold will also introduce new areas, new content (such as raids) and an increased level cap, building on the MMORPG's established expansion formula. Furthermore, Square Enix also revealed that Final Fantasy XIV has surpassed 35 million registered accounts worldwide, underlining the game's continued popularity since its relaunch as A Realm Reborn in 2013.

Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap With the emotional in-game closure on Dawntrail's story now having come and gone, the final leg of Final Fantasy 14 's Fanfest circuit has arrived in Tokyo with plenty more information to share on the upcoming Evercold expansion.

While details about the revamped gameplay, character customization, and Evercold's second combat job are some of the hottest topics on the stage, the biggest question is, of course, when exactly the expansion will drop.

From its gorgeous graphics to its timeless gameplay, here are ten reasons you need to play Final Fantasy Resonance right now.

Thanks to director Yoshi-P's opening keynote, Warriors of Light around the world now have a date to pencil in on their calendars. Or rather, there are a few dates to remember.

After showing off the final version of the trailer at the top of the keynote, Final Fantasy 14 director Naoki ("Yoshi-P") promptly announced that the Evercold expansion will now arrive a few weeks later on February 23, 2027 .

The reason for this, he explained, is that with all the major gameplay changes happening in Evercold (8.0), certain aspects of the development process took more time than initially anticipated, and he made the executive decision to implement an extension to ensure that the expansion will be truly polished for launch.

Initially, the game would have been "just barely" ready for the original launch date, but after finding several issues that still need addressing and to "bring the game to a level of quality we're satisfied with", the delay was necessary. After apologizing profusely, he assured that there would be no further delays beyond this February date.

However, for those who preorder the Evercold expansion, you'll be able to get in a few days early via its Early Access version on February 19, 2027 . As to how extensive that Early Access will be for players to explore, that wasn't clarified during the keynote, but more details will likely be revealed in a future Producer Live Letter livestream, as Yoshi-P said there will be several PLLs to go over everything in meticulous detail leading up to Evercold's launch.

Furthermore, Yoshi-P noted that an Evercold Benchmark test will become available sometime in December , allowing PC players in particular to test the specs of their current setups ahead of the expansion's launch, to ensure that the launch will be smooth sailing. As for the actual required PC system specs, those were not revealed in the Tokyo keynote.

Along with a concrete release date for the Evercold expansion, Yoshi-P has also announced when players will be able to place their pre-orders for all versions and platforms. Preorders will go live in just under a week on November 4, 2027 , on the official Square Enix website along with the respective websites for each major platform (Steam, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2).

Near the end of the keynote, Yoshi-P took the opportunity to review the physical Collector's Edition once again, showing the audience all the goodies included with the bundle.

At the forefront is, of course, the impressively detailed statue fashioned in the likeness of the Warrior of Light as a Reaper. Alongside that are a woven tapestry banner of the Fourth and two keychains. On top of all that, players will also get three different in-game items, including the Valhallar Odin Mount (a Final Fantasy 13 throwback), the Entreat Crystal Emote, and a set of Crystal Skyltborg weapons for Bastion.

items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV Online (Switch 2) - An Expansive Port That Demands Your Commitment
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Online has been through quite a rollercoaster journey over the years on its way to becoming one of the most respected MMOs in the industry. Its 2010 launch was a disaster, plagued with performance issues and shoddy design that torpedoed its reputation.

Rather than pulling the plug early, Square decided to swap in a new director to salvage it, leading to a reboot in 2013 called A Realm Reborn. Since then, the game has mostly gone from strength to strength across over a decade of expansions and is now in the process of building up its second major arc.

Though this isn’t the first time Square Enix has brought Final Fantasy XIV to console, it is the first time it’s come to a Nintendo platform, and I’m happy to report that it stuck the landing. The full fat experience is here in all its glory, giving you access to a high quality and addictive RPG experience that’s sure to be in the running for one of the most content-rich games ever produced for a handheld.

The narrative places you in the role of a self-insert character in the land of Eorzea who comes into the picture just as geopolitical tensions are on the rise. After a catastrophic war five years earlier, the expansionist Garlean Empire was repelled by the city-states comprising the Eorzean Alliance, but its leaders desire revenge and are winding up for another grab at ultimate control.

Amid this, you’re also told through a vision by a mysterious goddess of light named Hydaelyn that you’re her chosen champion, and she tasks you with finding six magical crystals to ward off the servants of an approaching darkness.

Thus, we set off on the early steps of what came to be called the Hydaelyn-Zodiark Saga, a four-part fantasy epic that should take you no less than two-hundred hours to complete, and that’s assuming that you beeline for the finale and engage in almost no side content. After all that, there’s then a whole other expansion that’s in the early stages of setting up the next ten-year arc.

Suffice to say, Final Fantasy XIV features one of the richest storylines available in a modern RPG, weaving together the subplots of various nations, factions, and supporting characters to make for an impressively complex and deep narrative.

The downside to this, however, is that the pacing can be all over the place. The 60-hour story of the base game alone is basically an extended exposition dump detailing all the major players in the world and setting the stage for the building conflict to come, meaning you spend a lot of time scrolling through line after line of unvoiced text from NPCs telling you about very interesting story beats that happened some other time offscreen.

This leads to a narrative experience with some incredible highs and disappointing lows. Once the plot picks up steam and starts focusing more on current events, there are lots of awesome character moments and payoffs that make all the time investment up to that point feel worth it. Yet between those moments, it can sometimes feel like the plot really takes its time focusing on largely irrelevant or uninteresting subjects that you simply have to endure to reach the good stuff.

Gameplay design follows the expected structure of an MMO, giving you an enormous living world to explore packed with jobs and levels to grind, side quests to fulfill, minigames to fool around with, dungeons to raid, and a massive story to gradually uncover.

As long as you stick to the Main Story Quest chain, you'll be toured around all the main points of interest in an area and progressively introduced to core mechanics and objectives at a measured pace. Side quest content then fills out the world with more detail and texture, though tons of the quest objectives admittedly boil down to 'bring me three boar skins' fetch quests.

A big part of what makes the gameplay loop so addicting is the versatility of your character, who can independently level dozens of jobs that fill out various combat and non-combat roles. In a combat role, your job is built around a growing variety of cooldown-based actions, echoing the classic Final Fantasy ATB system that blends turn-based and action gameplay.

Every combat job has its own distinct gimmicks and features, such as how the Thaumaturge operates by repeatedly shifting between two passive states that bolster either damage output or MP regeneration. Mechanics like this keep fights from feeling too much like you’re just watching cooldown icons on a hotbar, and there are enough distinguishing traits to make the various classes all feel like they’re worth experimenting with.

Non-combat roles are just as dynamic, even without the pressure of attacking foes. If you're working as a Goldsmith, you can create various bits of armour and jewellery, and it's much more involved than merely clicking the 'Craft' button on a menu after you have the materials.

London (31 st October, 2026) – During the FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo, SQUARE ENIX® announced that its critically acclaimed MMORPG FINAL FANTASY XIV Online has reached more than 35 million registered accounts globally and revealed new information about Evercold , the newest expansion set to release on Tuesday 23 rd February, 2027. During the opening keynote, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed “zephyr,” the second of two new jobs arriving in Evercold . A physical ranged DPS, zephyr joins the fray using a combination of crossbow shots and support from an avian familiar known as Nephele. A trailer showcasing the zephyr in action can be seen here: https://youtu.be/qX5jtcXjmts The keynote also introduced the full-length trailer for Evercold , which can be seen here: https://youtu.be/4qHEQ2CyOoA

Alongside the release date, Yoshida revealed that pre-orders for the Evercold expansion and the previously announced Collector’s Box will start beginning Wednesday 4 November. 2026 at 9:00 a.m. GMT. The Collector’s Bundle will be available for pre-order in limited quantities exclusively from the Square Enix Store and contains the physical Collector’s Box and a code for the FINAL FANTASY XIV: Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition for Windows® or Mac. PlayStation®5, PlayStation®4, XBOX Series X|S, Nintendo Switch™ 2 and Steam players can order the Collector’s Box as a standalone product and pre-order the Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition separately on their respective platforms. The Evercold Collector’s Box includes the physical goods listed below and does not include a copy of Evercold , in-game items, or pre-order bonuses.

For more information and the latest updates on Evercold , please visit the teaser site at: https://eu.finalfantasyxiv.com/evercold/ The keynote presentation (English language supported) is available to view on YouTube via the Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo Day 1 live stream: https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2915321914?t=1h32m44s

Conceived, written and directed by Hideaki Anno, EVANGELION:1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 were all hugely successful, captivating new fans and garnering much praise from a wide range of audiences. Though such an anniversary event was a first for the series, it proved to be a resounding success, attracting a great many visitors from Japan and around the world. The game is universally regarded as a landmark title of the RPG genre. The original title received high praise for its epic storyline, unique characters, and movie sequences that utilized the most cutting-edge technology of the time. Since then, the game revolving around iconic hero Cloud Strife and his pursuit of the antagonist Sephiroth has sold over 15.7 million copies worldwide and continues to receive widespread acclaim from critics and fans around the world. The popular game has expanded into spin-offs, films and merchandise. Now, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY VII Remake Series, created by a team of original and new developers, retells the story of the genre-redefining RPG across three distinct games. The first game of the trilogy, FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE, is available for PS4® consoles. The expanded edition, FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE, and the second entry, FINAL FANTASY VII REBIRTH, are now available for Nintendo Switch 2, XBOX Series X|S, XBOX PC, PS5® consoles and PC. items.content:
Keybound Brawler, a new event that tests your typing prowess, is coming to the Manderville Gold Saucer! The first iteration of the event will be a special collaboration with the FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE series. Participate in the collaboration stages to obtain MGC which can be exchanged for numerous rewards, including collaboration attire, a mount, emote, and more!

Event Duration

From Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 19:00 (AEDT) to the release of Patch 8.0 * The end date listed on Steam does not reflect the release date for Patch 8.0.

How to Participate

Begin the quest "Keyward Bound" by speaking to the Catlike Mammet in The Gold Saucer (X:5.4 Y:7.0). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy." * Players must first complete the quest "It Could Happen to You" to be able to travel to the Manderville Gold Saucer via airship from any of the three city-states. * Please note that a keyboard is required to participate in this content. Gamepads and on-screen keyboards cannot be used.

Rewards

* After this collaboration event has ended, it will be held as a special event at irregular intervals. Visit the special site for more details.

items.content:
We are delighted to announce that the Fall Guys collaboration will be blundering back to a realm near you very soon! Join a Blunderville show and get your hands on a whole host of exquisite prizes, including fetching attire, a marvelous mount, framer's kits, and more!

Event Duration

From Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 19:00 (AEDT) to Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / Wednesday, 28 October at 1:59 (AEDT)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "It Could Happen to You" by speaking to the Well-heeled Youth in Ul'dah – Steps of Nald (X:9.6 Y:9.0). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy." * Players can travel to the Manderville Gold Saucer via airship from any of the three city-states upon completing this quest.

Rewards

* This event is identical to the one previously held. * Players who have already completed the quest during a previous event release may immediately resume playing the collaboration content. * After this collaboration event has ended, it will be held as a special event at irregular intervals. Visit the special site for more details.

items.content:
The FINAL FANTASY XV collaboration event, A Nocturne for Heroes, returns. Don’t miss out on rewards like the Regalia Type-G 4-seater mount, the Lucian Prince costume set, Modern Aesthetics - Lucian Locks, orchestrion rolls, and more! * This event is identical to the one previously held. * If you have already completed the event, you can replay the quests via the seasonal event replay feature. To learn more about this feature, please check the special site.

Event Duration

From Thursday, September 24, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9;00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Tuesday, October 13, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Wednesday, 14 October at 1:59 (AEDT)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "The Man in Black" by speaking to Kipih Jakkya in Ul’dah, Steps of Nald (X:8.5 Y:9.7). * Players must be level 50 and above to start the quest. * Players must have completed the main scenario quest “The Ultimate Weapon.”

Rewards

Visit the special site for more details.

items.content: Faced with the coming Solstice, the fate Halmarut claims to await all worlds, the Warrior of Light embarks upon another journey─one that promises to grow ever colder... Patch 7.56 also introduces the new limited job beastmaster and its exclusive duty, the Crucible of the Unbroken. Furthermore, weekly restrictions have been removed and the Echo enabled in AAC Heavyweight Tier (Savage). Read the full patch notes on the Lodestone.
